## Changes since `v0.7.0`

### Features

- say Caps Lock is on in words beside the cursor for a moment: at a password prompt Caps Lock only turned the key into an up arrow, a mark a new user may not read; when Caps Lock turns on, or is already on as the prompt appears, the words now stand in the stars' place for two and a half seconds and then leave the mark alone, not cut short by typing since the key that reveals Caps Lock is often the first one typed; like the stars they move onto a chip when the row has no room, counting wide characters as two cells ([36c1dd42](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/36c1dd420a4989683e68cc5f14c333db965ec691))
- show a * beside the cursor for each character typed at a password prompt: nothing echoed what was typed at a sudo prompt, so a new user could not tell whether the keys arrived, and the Caps Lock warning sat far from where they looked; like sudo-rs's pwfeedback on Ubuntu 26.04, tTerm now draws a key beside the cursor and a * per typed character, counted from the keys sent and drawn over the terminal so nothing reaches the remote, with the key turned into a Caps Lock mark while that is on; the saved-password bar shows only when it offers something, closing it leaves the user to type, and the password_feedback setting, which backups and sync carry, turns the marks off to show only the key ([48a8ea53](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/48a8ea53ef269dffd8f42dac50a00bd127f09eab))
- mark a tab that waits for a password: a session stopped at a sudo or doas prompt showed nothing outside its own terminal, so a prompt in a background tab or another pane held up its command unnoticed; such a tab, its pane header and its row in the overflow panel now carry a key, which takes the warning color while Caps Lock is on and comes before an agent's mark or the news dot, since nothing runs on until the prompt is answered ([c1d32d76](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c1d32d7693f9bcdde45f93457ddb629ce17fc941))
- warn of Caps Lock in password fields: Caps Lock left on is the commonest reason a typed password is refused, and nothing said it was on; a field holding a hidden password now shows a Caps Lock mark beside its reveal toggle while it has the focus, the SSH sign-in prompt asks for passwords through that same field and so gains the reveal toggle too, and WebKit's own indicator on macOS is hidden so the mark does not show twice ([773e7b09](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/773e7b09d09e1afd89c7b61dbe5215c5cb77afdd))
- back up and sync how the connections panel lists profiles: the By group / Last used switch was kept only in this device's local storage, so neither a backup nor WebDAV sync carried it; it is now the profile_sort setting in the config file, which backups take with the other settings, and it is among the settings sync shares, since listing by last use means the same on every device ([bd7855e2](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/bd7855e2d939ea817a8427e70ad32cfc41a6eaa0))
- copy and paste in the terminal with Ctrl+Shift+C / V, and show them in its context menu: the menu's Copy and Paste showed no shortcut, since neither was a keymap action, and from the keyboard copying and pasting were left to whatever the webview did with a chord xterm passes on, which for Ctrl+Shift+C is likely inspecting an element rather than copying; both are now keymap actions, bound to Ctrl+Shift+C / V on Windows and Linux and left unbound on macOS, where Cmd+C / V already copy and paste and Cmd+V uploads to SFTP, and they serve only a focused terminal so a text field elsewhere keeps the chord ([c03baf98](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c03baf9836ce8868b4e2ee30f78335f47e7e02cd))
- put the saved connection a search fits best first: matches were listed in their saved order, so typing a connection's full name could leave it below others that only matched its user, and the launcher, which shows eight, could cut it off; a match on the name itself now comes first, then the start of the name or of a word in it, then every word in the name or the start of the host, then a match anywhere else, with the connection used last first among equals; the launcher ranks before it cuts, and the panel ranks its recent list and, by group, each group and the order of the groups, so Enter opens the best fit ([901544d8](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/901544d81c18af555b23487f5c2134141174f967))
- list the connections panel by last use: with many groups, the connections used every day were spread over all of them; a switch beside the search now lists every connection in one list, the one used last first and the ones never used after in the saved order, each row naming its group, while By group keeps the groups as they were; the choice is remembered on this device ([a8460754](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/a846075420c9b988e5af858f3984abdd8370c014))
- list the saved connections used lately in the new tab launcher: its recents held only quick connections, so a saved connection opened every day had to be searched for each time; a saved connection now counts as used each time one of its tabs connects, SSH or serial, the launcher lists it among the recents with the quick connections, newest first, and a search puts the saved connections used lately before the others; like the other recents they stay on this device, are not synced, and go into backups with the settings ([f9bc8e35](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/f9bc8e35842c3f9c429862e1f0c9e8044e8e5ff1))
- badge a WSL tab's distribution logo as local: with the logo, a WSL Ubuntu tab looked just like an SSH tab to an Ubuntu host; a WSL tab showing a distribution's logo, reported or picked, now carries a small inverted square with a prompt in its corner, a square so it is not taken for the attention dots beside it, while SSH tabs and glyph icons stay as they were ([c3be0d39](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c3be0d398aa25a7856422814feebc9b6bd7c3709))
- show a WSL tab's distribution logo: a WSL tab always showed the same orange terminal icon, whichever distribution it ran, while an SSH tab showed its host's logo; the WSL launcher now reports the ID, ID_LIKE and NAME from os-release as it starts the shell (OSC 777 ; tterm-os), the tab keeps the distribution it names and shows its logo, under any icon the user picked for WSL or for the tab, and a restored tab shows it before WSL is up ([3f10e364](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/3f10e3648e8878195cbb2eef773c973a213a7c19))
- restore each terminal tab's content after a restart: a restored tab opened on an empty terminal, so what it had shown before tTerm closed was gone; under General, Startup, Restore terminal content after a restart, off by default, now keeps each terminal's main screen and scrollback down to its cursor, up to 5000 lines with colors but without modes or a full-screen program's screen, saves the terminals that changed every 10 seconds and once more before a quit or a relaunch, and shows it again above the tab's new session under a dim line with when it was saved; turning it off deletes what was saved, importing a session from a backup drops it so the imported tabs never show another tab's content, and the setting syncs with the others ([b6de1341](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/b6de134120e2984373ae12b1a09ed90a49127803))
- let the UI save before the app quits: every quit, from the tray, the window, Cmd+Q or the tunnels' confirmation, ended the webview at once, so what it kept only in memory was lost; once the UI says it has something to save, a quit now tells it with app-will-quit and waits up to 1.5 seconds for its answer, a second quit while waiting goes ahead at once, and without anything to save a quit is as immediate as before ([b6bb8fdd](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/b6bb8fddf087ac73bc3900fd9dc463e9f0148bef))
- keep each terminal tab's content on disk for the next launch: a restart showed every tab empty, as nothing kept what its terminal had shown; each tab's content can now be saved as a gzip file under scrollback/ in the config folder, owner-only on Unix and outside the database so backups and sync never carry it, read back for the tabs of the restored session, and deleted once its tab is no longer in the saved session or the session is cleared ([42ffbb4f](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/42ffbb4f18079fbb399b0eec979478b31fb5b57c))
- add an islands window style: the content sat flush under the title bar, and split panes were set apart by lines; under Appearance, Interface, Window style can now be Islands, which runs the title bar's color around the content as the window's ground and floats each pane, and the empty page, on it as a rounded card, with split panes told apart by the gap between them and dividers drawn only when pointed at; over the window blur the ground takes a lighter tint and the cards still come to the set opacity; the style is remembered for the next launch so it starts without the classic layout first, and it syncs with the other settings ([3c182500](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/3c182500da8075ca9bd22a3606c87b6cd7d83a66))
- add split layout templates: a tab could only be split one pane at a time, and a layout built up that way had to be built again for the next tab; Split Layout… in a tab's or a pane's menu, or a shortcut left unbound, now lays the tab out as one of six built-in layouts or one saved from a split tab, with its sizes; panes the layout adds open copies of the chosen pane, panes it has no room for move out into tabs of their own, and saved layouts sync and can be deleted there or under Appearance, Split panes ([de082cca](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/de082ccac25377b2863251adbb3da166a2f8538d))
- add settings for how split panes look: each pane of a split tab always showed a header, and every pane looked alike whichever had the keyboard; under Appearance, Split panes, the headers can now be turned off, which marks the pane with the keyboard by a thin accent frame instead, and the panes without the keyboard can fade by 15, 30 or 45 percent, neither while a pane is zoomed; the settings sync with the others ([48d9ecd0](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/48d9ecd002fb5b70e32926b8084f1bea3fc01a6c))
- let the overflow menu find sessions in split tabs: it searched only the pane each tab of the bar had the focus in, so a session in another pane of a split tab could not be found; now it lists the panes of a split tab under it, a search keeps a tab when it or any of its panes matches and lists the panes that do, and picking a pane, or Enter on one, goes straight to it ([cc949b8e](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/cc949b8e0ba66a94e8ba5d91c7e0bd900c8d1d68))
- make each tab in the bar hold its own split layout, as iTerm2 and Windows Terminal do: a split tab showed in the tab bar and again in every pane group's tab strip, so the same session sat in two rows of tabs; now a tab of the bar holds one or more panes laid out by its own split tree, the bar shows it once with its pane count and the marks of all its panes, and each pane of a split tab gets a slim header that names it and splits, zooms, unsplits or closes it; dragging a pane moves it beside another or, onto the tab bar, out into a tab of its own, dragging a tab onto a pane merges its panes there, a pane zooms like tmux on Mod+Alt+Enter, Mod+Alt+\\ now unsplits a tab into one tab per pane, the close chord closes the active pane and closing a tab of several sessions asks first; Dockview gives way to a layout of our own that keeps every pane mounted and sized while hidden, so switching tabs or moving panes between them never remounts or refits a terminal, and sessions save the layout in a new format, moving older Dockview layouts over on restore ([2e75e196](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/2e75e1968e661fc0bbb2a6fe9857696312c7310e))
- show the macOS icon on a macOS host's SSH tabs: the probe only read /etc/os-release, which macOS lacks, so its tabs got no icon; it now falls back to sw_vers and runs under sh -s, since a csh login shell took its 2>/dev/null for an argument and reported nothing ([ea096fc9](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/ea096fc9d6e41fdc81d59526ef3d5b745b019eee))
- monitor macOS and FreeBSD hosts, not only Linux: the script now has a section per system and runs under sh -s, so csh and fish login shells work too; FreeBSD reads CPU ticks, memory pages and the ZFS cache from sysctl and swap from swapinfo, while macOS reads memory as Activity Monitor counts it from vm_stat and measures the CPU over one second with iostat, since it keeps no tick counters and top costs almost a second of CPU per sample; both read the default interface's netstat counters and df with mount, where APFS volumes report their container's usage, hidden macOS volumes are skipped and ZFS datasets fold into one row per pool; other systems get a translated message naming them instead of the English-only "Only Linux hosts are supported", and FreeBSD and macOS get icons of their own ([e258b797](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/e258b7975b12ec01f82687c68d5b1833f9e2658a))
- duplicate the active tab from the keyboard with Mod+Shift+D: copying a terminal took a trip to its context menu, while renaming and closing already had chords; the new tabs.duplicateActive action follows Windows Terminal's Ctrl+Shift+D, can be rebound or unbound in the keymap settings, shows beside Duplicate Tab in the tab bar's and split group's menus, and lets the chord through on page tabs and remote file editors, which cannot be copied ([9a67a60e](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/9a67a60ef1f382ee57396bef87426d6ce97c7bc1))

### Fixes

- move password feedback off the cursor's row when the row has no room for it: the key and stars started a cell after the cursor and were cut to fit what was left of the row, so near its end the stars shrank to an ellipsis and at the last column the key was drawn past the terminal's edge and clipped; with fewer than eight cells to spare they now go on a chip on the row above, or below on the first row, pulled left to end within the row and drawn on the terminal's background, and the saved-password bar keeps clear of that chip too ([2996738f](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/2996738f12432a6e6ef37753b17e229c997e0fff))
- match each word of a connection search on its own: the connections panel looked for the whole query as one run of text in the joined fields, so "web root" found nothing for a connection named web-01 with the user root, while the new tab launcher found it; the panel now matches the way the launcher does, every word anywhere in the name, group, host, username, connection type or serial port, and its placeholder names the username it already searched ([738caf30](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/738caf30b30e76c5eb5a6e034e486488ecf795b7))
- upload a file dropped on an SFTP drawer to the pane under the cursor, not to another tab: the window drop listener was registered again on every directory change, and when it was cleaned up before its registration finished it was never stopped, so it kept uploading every later drop into the directory of the tab it was made for, whichever tab was in front; a listener that arrives after its cleanup is now stopped at once, it is registered only as the drawer opens, and the drawer in the pane under the cursor takes the drop, since a file dragged in from another window leaves the focus on the pane clicked last, while a drop outside every pane still goes to the focused drawer ([cb5a9eeb](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/cb5a9eeb61a3dd15165aa7e414377ee4d02edf23))
- end a bracketed paste a Ctrl+C cuts short: a Ctrl+C stops what is still queued of a paste, and with it the marker that ends a bracketed paste, so the program kept taking whatever was typed next for more of the paste; the end marker is now written before the Ctrl+C, after the unread input of a Windows console is discarded so that the discard does not drop it as well ([6daf85b8](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/6daf85b813f65ee6ae4f4b97cfcd0cca9f8063e9))
- find the network interface on a Linux host without the ip command: the /proc/net/dev fallback took the file's header line for an interface, so such hosts, like slim Debian images, showed no network traffic; it now skips the two header lines ([c9fb7271](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c9fb7271ec996657738feeadde3c7a0450e7379a))

### Performance

- write a bracketed paste at once instead of pacing it: a large paste into Claude Code took a second or more to show, since a paste was written only as fast as the program answered it with output, and a program that turned on bracketed paste, as Claude Code and zsh do, holds the whole paste silently until its end, so each doubling of the window waited out a 100 ms stall; a paste starting with the bracketed paste marker is now written straight away, while one without it is still paced so that a Ctrl+C can stop it ([dd1e15d7](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/dd1e15d772ef92af16d20a12f539261d7d2fefbe))
- send terminal output that follows a pause at once: every read opened an 8 ms batching window before it went to the webview, so the echo of each keystroke waited out the window, and on Windows, whose timer ticks about every 15.6 ms, the wait came to nearly 19 ms; output arriving a full window after the last batch now goes out immediately, while output inside a burst still coalesces, in a window that ends one interval after the previous batch ([34052045](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/34052045321a4676ae8386be87d5b0be36554270))

### UI and usability

- tint a tab out of view while it waits for a password: the 12px key was the only mark, easy to miss among many tabs while sudo gives up after a few minutes; such a tab now carries a tint and border in the key's color, drawn over its background so hover still shows, and the active tab keeps its look since its terminal shows the prompt already ([d4f7430d](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/d4f7430da877efea0380cb9510189ce3d0e58021))
- fold the custom prompt patterns away and shorten the star setting's text: the password prompts section opened on a regular expression field and on a description of sudo's pwfeedback that few people need; the star switch now says only what it shows, and the patterns sit under Advanced: password prompt detection, folded by default behind a line saying sudo, sudo-rs and doas are recognized already and how many custom patterns are added ([c339aa5b](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c339aa5b15eeb97982d57d9b8c0426a1a1303aec))
- keep the saved-password bar readable in a narrow pane and off the prompt line: the bar sat on one row with its buttons fixed in width, so in a narrow pane the line naming whose password would be sent shrank to an ellipsis, and the bar spread across the bottom row where the prompt usually is; its buttons now wrap onto a second row when the text would get less than about 16em, and it moves to the top-right corner whenever at the bottom it would cover the prompt line up to the key beside the cursor ([8a72763f](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/8a72763f665546bf9024310d480405abe3f7eb7f))
- shorten the restored-content line back to a short dim mark: the line across the whole terminal drew the eye away from the new session, and wrapped once the window narrowed; it is again a short dash on each side of the text, keeping the 24-hour time, which now leads with the year when the content was saved in another year ([5576dc71](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/5576dc71cdcce3ae500ef15587cf785ce0b6b2ae))
- draw the restored-content line across the terminal with a 24-hour time: the line under a tab's restored content was a short dash pair around the text, with the time in the system's 12-hour form; it now runs the full width of the terminal with the text in its middle, wide characters counted as two cells, and the time reads like 10-25 14:03; the content is written once the terminal has settled on its size, just before its session starts, so the line matches the terminal's width ([b8ffe664](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/b8ffe6648f01ebbfa5bc001af963b23da75d0242))
- mark the active pane of a split tab the way the tab bar marks its active tab: a 2px strip down the header's left edge was easy to miss, so the header now draws what runs in the pane as a tab of its own, which in the active pane takes the active tab's fill and a top accent only as wide as its title, capped at 320px, instead of a stripe across the whole pane ([cca6f84a](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/cca6f84a330b09c3a8f811d08de2d36a17602923))

### Other changes

- say what the saved-password button does and stop saying nothing shows: the tab's tooltip still claimed nothing appears while typing a password, which the * marks beside the cursor now contradict, and the bar's Fill button read as filling the field for a check when it sends the password and presses Enter; the tooltip now only says to press Enter when done, the button, its shortcut and the profile setting say the password is submitted, and closing the bar says the user types it instead ([8841b19f](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/8841b19f0ad8c7ab383aa401eecc0dc019abacad))
- read FreeBSD tick groups with as_chunks: clippy 1.99 flags chunks_exact with a constant size, and the fixed-size groups also let each one destructure into its five states instead of indexing ([bcef8c42](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/bcef8c422514aa5a78410437c807abecc43780a2))
